1_incident_name: Delaware Bay Container Vessel Collision & Fuel Oil Spill

4_map_sketch.total_area_of_operations: 6.0-mile radius centered at Delaware Bay Shipping Channel Buoy 14 near Lewes, DE.
4_map_sketch.incident_site_area: Delaware Bay Channel Buoy 14 (38.85°N, 75.12°W), where container vessel M/V Atlantic Voyager collided with a bulk carrier, breaching fuel tank #3 port side.
4_map_sketch.impacted_areas: 3.5-mile long heavy oil sheen extending East-Southeast across the bay channel towards Cape Henlopen State Park.
4_map_sketch.threatened_areas: Prime Hook National Wildlife Refuge (4.0 miles Northwest) and Cape Henlopen Tidal Salt Marshes (2.5 miles South).
4_map_sketch.overflight_results: USCG HC-144 Ocean Sentry aircraft confirmed a 300-yard wide slick of Intermediate Fuel Oil (IFO 380) drifting with the flood tide.
4_map_sketch.trajectories: Waterborne oil slick migrating East-Southeast at 2.2 knots toward Cape Henlopen under coastal winds of 14 knots from West-Northwest.
4_map_sketch.impacted_shorelines: 2.0 miles of outer sandy beach and dune lines along Cape Henlopen State Park.
4_map_sketch.graphics_and_symbology: North oriented vertically, depicting Staging Area Echo at Lewes Ferry Terminal, Incident Command Post at USCG Sector Delaware Bay Headquarters, 1,000-yard Maritime Safety Zone, Boom Sites 1, 2, and 3, and wildlife protection zones.

5_situation_summary_health_safety_briefi.situation_summary: At 22:15 EDT on 06/29/2026, container vessel M/V Atlantic Voyager collided with anchored bulk carrier M/V Pacific Trader near Buoy 14. Port fuel tank #3 breached, discharging approximately 25,000 gallons of heavy Intermediate Fuel Oil (IFO 380) before internal fuel transfer halted the release.
5_situation_summary_health_safety_briefi.health_and_safety_hazards: Hydrocarbon vapor exposure (benzene/H2S), direct dermal toxicity, severe slip hazards on oily vessel hulls and shorelines, nighttime over-water operations, water drowning risk, and wildlife exposure risks.
5_situation_summary_health_safety_briefi.necessary_measures: Establish 1,000-yard Maritime Safety Zone; mandatory Level C PPE with PFDs and half-mask organic vapor respirators for maritime responders; continuous H2S and PID air monitoring on response vessels; compulsory work-rest hydration cycles; mobile vessel decontamination station established at Lewes Pier.

7_current_and_planned_objectives: Secure maritime safety perimeter and stabilize damaged vessel by 01:00 hours.
Deploy protective booming across Cape Henlopen salt marsh inlets by 04:00 hours.
Initiate offshore skimming operations using MSRC oil recovery vessels by 05:30 hours.
Activate wildlife rescue and rehab operations with Tri-State Bird Rescue by 06:00 hours.
Establish Unified Command (USCG, EPA, Delaware DNREC, M/V Atlantic Voyager RP) by 02:00 hours.

8_current_and_planned_actions_strategies.actions: Initial alarm dispatch; USCG Station Lewes response boats 45601 and 45602 respond to establish maritime safety zone.
Local Command established by Captain P. Hayes; Sector Delaware Bay requests MSRC oil spill response vessel mobilization.
M/V Atlantic Voyager crew completes internal fuel transfer, halting active discharge from fuel tank #3.
USCG HC-144 overflight completes IR sensor oil slick mapping.
Delaware DNREC response team arrives at Lewes Command Post; Unified Command established.
Planned: MSRC Response Vessel Delaware Responder deploys 2,500 feet of ocean containment boom at Buoy 14.
Planned: Deploy sorbent diversion boom at Cape Henlopen Inlet (Boom Site 2).
Planned: Tri-State Bird Rescue team commences shoreline wildlife search along Cape Henlopen beaches.

incident_commanders: Captain P. Hayes (USCG Unified Command IC)

10_resource_summary.notes: Maintaining 1,000-yard safety zone around damaged vessel.
Conducting water sampling and perimeter safety watch.
Deployed 2,500 ft ocean boom and preparing offshore skimmer.
Completed IR slick mapping and overflight tracking.
En route to establish bird cleaning station at Lewes Pier.
Mobilizing for Cape Henlopen beach oil assessment.
